plugin.name: Physics
plugin.description: Groups and components as rigid bodies that fall, bounce, slide and collide – hinges, sliders, motors with programs, ropes and springs for robot arms and machines, thrust, lift and air for things that fly, water that floats bodies, a liquid and a wind tunnel – without changing the model.

panel.title: Physics
panel.keepHint: Writes the places the bodies have now into the model (one undo step)
panel.startHint: Make groups or components bodies, then start – the model stays as it is. Reset and Keep work once it has started.
panel.period: Back and forth (s, 0 = on and on)
panel.jointHint: Choose a joint, take the joint tool and click a face of the body (a hinge turns around the face's normal), then the body it holds on to – or empty space for the world.
panel.selectHint: Select a group or component to make it a body, a region or to give it joints.
panel.stepHint: Pauses and goes a tenth of a second further – watch it step by step
panel.resetHint: Back to the start: the bodies show where the model has them

typeHints.none: Plain groups are part of the still world everything collides with.
typeHints.dynamic: Falls, bounces, slides and is pushed – by gravity, forces, joints and other bodies.
typeHints.static: Stays where it is; others collide with its exact faces.
typeHints.kinematic: Moves and turns at its own speed and pushes what is in its way – a lift, a turntable, a piston.
typeHints.off: Not part of the simulation: nothing collides with it.
typeHints.water: Its box is water up to its top: bodies float by their density and drift with the current.
typeHints.liquid: Its box is filled with drops at the start that flow around and over everything.
typeHints.tunnel: Its box is a wind tunnel: the air flows around everything in it, shown by smoke lines.

tools.pullStatus: Drag a body while the simulation runs – it follows on a spring.
tools.jointStatusFirst: {kind}: click a face of the body that gets the joint.
tools.jointStatusSecond: {kind}: click the body it holds on to – the same body for the group it lies in, empty space for the world. Esc cancels.
tools.pullMiss: No dynamic body there – press on a body that falls (not a static one) and drag
tools.jointAdded: {kind} on {name}, held by {to} – set it up in the Physics panel

commands.keep: Keep the places of the simulation

errors.load: The physics engine could not be loaded: {error}
errors.vector: "{name}" must be three numbers [x, y, z]
errors.jointOnGroup: A joint needs a group or component – click one of its faces

script.body: Makes a group or component a body (dynamic, static, kinematic, off) or a region (water, liquid, tunnel) with its material, shape, start speed and forces – or changes it. Returns the instance id.
script.joint: Adds a joint to a body: hinge, slider, ball, fixed, rope or spring – to another group, the group it lies in or the world, with limits, a motor and a program. Points and axes in model coordinates.
script.settings: Gravity, wind, air drag, the ground and the speed of the simulation – returns the settings.
script.start: Starts the simulation once the script is done – `at` seconds simulated at once, `pause` to stay there.
script.bodies: Every body and region in the model with its data.
script.remove: Makes a body a plain group again.

guide.title: Physics guide
guide.open: How does it work? Open the guide
guide.heading: Your first simulation
guide.intro: Step by step through the plugin. Every step ticks itself off once you have done it – the buttons do it for you or take the right tool.

actions.editJoint: Open the joint in the panel

practice.title: Something to try it on
practice.text: Physics works on groups and components. Build a practice scene – three crates, a ball and a door (it replaces the model) – or use your own groups.
practice.done: There are groups in the model.

bodies.title: Make them bodies
bodies.text: Only bodies take part. Select the groups (or click “Select all groups”), then “Selection → dynamic” – or in the Physics panel under “What should it do?” click “Falls”: they fall, bounce and collide. Below it you choose what they are made of.

start.title: Start
start.text:
Start the simulation – here, in the Physics panel or from the command palette. The first time the engine loads for a moment.
The model itself does not change: the bodies are only shown where they are.

controls.title: Pause, step, reset
controls.text: Pause stops it where it is, Go on continues. Step pauses and goes a tenth of a second further – press it a few times. Reset puts everything back to the start (only while it runs or is paused).

pull.title: Pull bodies
pull.text:
Take the Pull tool (it starts the simulation), then press the mouse button on a falling body and drag: it follows the pointer on a spring, as if on a rubber band. Static bodies cannot be pulled.
In the physics mode the tool is in the toolbar on the left.

joint.title: A hinge
joint.text:
Take the hinge tool. 1st click: a face of the body that gets the hinge – the hinge turns around that face’s normal, so for a door click its top face, near the end where it should hang (it snaps to the corner, a dot shows it). 2nd click: empty space (the hinge holds on to the world) or another body.
Then start: the door swings instead of falling over.

motor.title: A motor
motor.text: Open the joint in the Physics panel: in the simple view tick “Motor” next to the hinge – it turns on and on. The advanced view has a target in degrees, a speed or a program such as 0:0, 2:90, 4:0 (seconds:degrees, repeated), and a slider to drive it by hand while it runs.

keep.title: Keep the places
keep.text: Let things fall into place, then Keep: the places the bodies have now are written into the model – one undo step. Useful to scatter crates or let a pile settle.

more.title: More: the demos
more.text: The demos show what else it can do – robot arms on programs, ropes and springs, flight, water, a liquid and a wind tunnel. Each one opens in the script editor; Run builds it (it replaces the model) and starts it. All are in the script editor’s examples under Physics.

basic.nothing: Click an object to say what it should do. It has to be a group or component.
basic.loose: These are loose faces – physics needs a group.
basic.otherKind: It has a kind from the advanced view (moving, water …) – change it there.
basic.attachHint: Nothing – it falls freely. Attach it to the world or to another object:
basic.attachSteps:
1. Click a face of this object near where it should hold (it snaps to a corner or the middle).
2. Click empty space to hold on to the world, or another object.
Esc cancels.
basic.more: Water, wind, liquids, motor programs and exact values are in the advanced view.
basic.pushHint: Directions as you see it now: away is into the view.
basic.pushed: It starts moving – the blue arrow shows where.
basic.attachStepsHinge:
1. Click the object near the edge it should hang on – the hinge stands upright there (a dot shows where).
2. Click empty space to hold it on the world, or another object (a frame).
Esc cancels.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.empty: Start it – what happens is recorded here, and you can drag back to any moment.
timeline.rewound: An earlier moment – Go on or Step simulates again from here.

record.hint: Records the 3D view as a video (MP4 or WebM) – it starts the simulation if it is not running
